first_impression.reaction: My assistant forwarded it because Queenstown came up as a summer option for the Sydney side of the family. The first screen is calm and answers the legal question in two sentences. There's no sales talk and no prices. Most of it is a self-service guide for two Australians, down to driving licences and bar ID, which isn't my world. Her summary would be 'legally simple, 3-day licence window, name a back-up venue, real quake and weather risk, and a good list of lodge questions at the end'. I read the takeaways, the personalised or registry part, the hazards paragraph, the regions, the venues section and the close.

journey.reaction: Dry and direct. No gushing. That's the tone I'd want from anyone advising my family.

journey.quote: Yes, you can get married in New Zealand as Australians, and you do not need to be New Zealand citizens: visitors to New Zealand can marry there.
journey.reaction: We're between Dubai, Sydney and London. The page assumes two Australian passports, so my assistant has to work out what still applies to us.

journey.quote: The licence must be in place at least 3 working days before the wedding, lasts 3 months, and only covers the venues you name on it, so name a back-up.
journey.reaction: Useful and short. The venue being written into the licence is exactly the sort of detail that catches people out. It goes in the file.

journey.quote: A registry ceremony suits couples who want the legal marriage done quietly, with the celebration held separately.
journey.reaction: This is how I'd do it. A private legal signing with family only, then the large celebration somewhere we control.

journey.section: Practical notes for you and your guests
journey.quote: An Australian driver's licence is not approved ID for buying alcohol or entering licensed premises, so guests heading to a bar after the reception should carry their passport.
journey.reaction: Bar ID for guests. Over-explaining for me. My guests won't be wandering off to a bar; this tells me the page is written for a different wedding.

journey.quote: When you arrive in New Zealand, you visit a registry office to sign a declaration before the ceremony, and the addresses are on the application form.
journey.reaction: We have to appear in person at a public office. Fine, but I'd want to know who arranges that quietly and whether it can be private. The page doesn't say whether anyone does this with us.

journey.section: When to get married in New Zealand
journey.quote: New Zealand has several active volcanoes, and alert levels can rise quickly, with evacuation ordered at short notice.
journey.reaction: Said plainly, which I respect. With 300 guests flying in, our people will want to know what the evacuation plan actually is. The venue questions below help, but only just.

journey.quote: If one of you is still planning the question, our [proposal spots in New Zealand](https://weddedwonderland.com/proposal-destinations-in-new-zealand) overlap with several of these regions.
journey.reaction: A bit cute and eager. It reads like content linking to content. Not for me.

journey.quote: Lodges, vineyard estates and private homes are the usual settings for a New Zealand wedding at this level, and each prices differently.
journey.reaction: Right settings, and no 'from' price, thank you. But 'at this level' arrives from nowhere. Nothing earlier talks about scale, so I'm not sure what level they mean.

journey.quote: **Sole use:** can we take the whole property for the nights we need, with no other guests or events alongside?
journey.reaction: The whole property, for nights. That's my question almost word for word.

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security work, and how would it work alongside a private team we bring?
journey.reaction: Whoever wrote this has met families like mine. Our team would work with theirs, and this is the right way to ask it.

journey.quote: **Privacy:** how do you handle other guests, drones and outside photographers during our events?
journey.reaction: Drones and outside photographers are where leaks come from. Good.

journey.quote: **Guest travel:** how do guests reach you from the nearest airport, and what happens if roads close?
journey.reaction: Right question, but for remote lodges I'd expect private transfers or helicopters to be mentioned, and who arranges them. The page leaves it with the venue.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One contact suits me; fewer people, fewer leaks. Fee in writing suits the family office. AUD and 'your time zone' assume I'm in Sydney, and nothing tells me they've done it at our size.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a New Zealand wedding for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee worked out, and do you earn commission from the lodges you book? (deferred business detail)
Who would actually be on the ground in New Zealand for us during the wedding week? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private transfers, charter flights or helicopters to remote lodges, and backup transport if roads close? (deferred business detail)
Would you handle the BDM 58 form, the registry office visit, the certificate and the Apostille for us, or are we expected to do it ourselves? (deferred business detail)
What access or perks come with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
Can a lodge or estate be closed to the public for several days for a guest list of this size, and are there properties that can sleep that many?
Does the process differ if one of us is not Australian, or if witnesses and guests hold other passports?
With earthquake, tsunami and volcano risk, what does a guest evacuation plan look like for a large wedding?
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, guest lists, no social media?
Can I work through my assistant or family office, and can you quote in another currency?

turn_offs_found.quote: An Australian driver's licence is not approved ID for buying alcohol or entering licensed premises, so guests heading to a bar after the reception should carry their passport.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Guest bar-ID advice makes the page read as written for couples doing everything themselves, not a family with staff.

turn_offs_found.quote: Medical facilities are of a similar standard to Australia's, and a reciprocal health care agreement lets Australians access public medical care by showing an Australian passport and a valid Medicare card.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining and Australia-only. Medicare is irrelevant to my family and makes the page feel like a standard traveller guide.

turn_offs_found.quote: If one of you is still planning the question, our [proposal spots in New Zealand](https://weddedwonderland.com/proposal-destinations-in-new-zealand) overlap with several of these regions.
turn_offs_found.why: Eager tone. A cross-promotional aside that cheapens an otherwise understated section.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the lodge questions (sole use, security, privacy, guest travel) and the 'name a back-up venue on the licence' point in the planning file, and forward the earthquake and volcano paragraph to our head of security. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=get-married-in-new-zealand&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public blog link. The lodge questions show you understand sole use, security and drones, which is more than most, but I'd want a private introduction and proof you've delivered at our size.

top_3_changes: Soften 'at this level' in 'Lodges, vineyard estates and private homes are the usual settings for a New Zealand wedding at this level' so it doesn't presume a scale the page never set up (for example 'for a larger or more private wedding').
Trim the over-explaining for readers who delegate: cut the bar-ID line and shorten the Medicare sentence to one line, and drop or move the proposal-spots aside out of the regions intro.

Link the hazard paragraph to planning: add a venue question about guest evacuation and private transfer arrangements for remote lodges, phrased as a question to ask, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.
